subject: Clarifying onshore fallback & operator vs processor clause for CCPA/CPRA
messages:
From: Sarah Liu <compliance@medisafe.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Raj Patel <it@medisafe.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick questions on CCPA role and onshore fallback timeline

Hi Kimberly / Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week — good discussion. As part of our procurement checklist we need to nail two items before legal will sign:

1) Confirmation that Redwood will be treated as a "Service Provider" (operator) under CCPA/CPRA and not a Seller for the datasets we send for inference;
2) A concrete onshore-fallback plan for telemetry and transient logs if we request onshore processing or if we trigger a regional outage (timeline, scope, and whether any subprocessors are involved).

Attached is our short RFI (Medisafe_RFI_DPA.xlsx) with the specific fields Legal/InfoSec need filled. Can you reply with wording you prefer in the addendum and an approximate SLA for onshore processing availability? We prefer examples or redline language that maps to the CPRA Exhibit.

Also, if you have a copy of the security bundle or SOC2 report we can share with our auditors, please include that or point me to a secure link.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if that helps.

Best,
Sarah Liu
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Medisafe

Attachments: Medisafe_RFI_DPA.xlsx (spreadsheet, 1 sheet)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Sarah Liu <compliance@medisafe.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick questions on CCPA role and onshore fallback timeline

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear RFI. Short answer up front: we accept the Service Provider / operator alignment under CCPA/CPRA for customer-provided data used for inference, subject to the narrow limited-use language in the DPA. Below is a suggested approach and a next-step schedule.

Summary (proposal):
- Role: Redwood will sign the US state privacy addendum confirming Service Provider / Operator treatment; we will not sell customer-provided data or use it for advertising purposes.
- Telemetry & onshore fallback: we offer a documented onshore-fallback option that can be invoked by contract or via a support SLA trigger. Standard response window: 48 hours to confirm onshore routing, 5 business days to enable reserved onshore capacity for transient telemetry retention, and up to 30 days for persistent onshore processing for large historic data migrations (example: customer requests full re-processing).
- Subprocessors: most infra subprocessors are cloud providers and network/CDN partners; we offer an onshore fallback map that removes offshore logging/analytics subprocessors where feasible (details in the attached DPA draft).

I've attached a working draft DPA excerpt with redline suggestions (redwood_dpa_draft_v2.docx). Rishi from Legal is looped in for specific clause language/brightlines on telemetry classification.

Proposed next steps:
1) We fill the RFI spreadsheet this afternoon and send you the draft addendum redline by EOD.
2) Schedule a 30-min call Thu 10am PT to walk the onshore-fallback operational flow with InfoSec.
3) Share SOC2 / security artifacts via our secure portal (link below) after an NDA page is accepted (we can provide time-limited access).

If that timeline works, I'll start the RFI responses now.

Cheers,
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0129
Redwood Inference

Related links: https://redwood.hubspot.com/deal/HD-4829

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2027 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick questions on CCPA role and onshore fallback timeline

Kim / Marissa — quick legal notes and ask for evidence before we sign off on the proposed wording:

1) Operator vs Processor: we'll commit to the Service Provider/operator definition. We need explicit contract language that excludes independent use and sets a narrow limited-use purpose clause. I'm proposing the following brightline in the addendum: "Redwood will not use, retain, or combine Customer Personal Data for purposes other than providing the Services and as necessary for security, debugging, and improving service reliability, in strictly aggregated or de-identified form."

2) Telemetry definition: the draft DPA must define telemetry classes (routing logs, usage metrics, payload logs, KV cache traces). For Medisafe, we recommend that payload logs and identifiable traces be classified as "transient telemetry" and subject to the onshore-fallback flow.

3) Subprocessors and emergency on-boarding: include a 7-day notice and approval window for any persistent offshore subprocessor that would handle payload-level telemetry. For emergency security subprocessors, we will provide post-facto notification within 48 hours and include contractual audit rights.

I'll attach our standard evidence bundle for SOC/Security references to share with the customer portal (security_evidence_bundle.zip). Suggest we redline the DPA and circulate to Sarah and Raj prior to the Thu call.

On the call, I'll walk the SLA triggers and fallback runbook.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Kim / Rishi — thanks for the fast turnaround and for the proposed language. A few quick items from our side:

- The brightline wording on limited use looks good; Legal wants one more pass to ensure "de-identified" is HHS-level de-id (we'll propose minor edits).
- For telemetry, Raj asked that payload logs be treated as high-sensitivity and that any onshore-fallback activation include a confirmation step and a runbook excerpt showing where logs will be retained and for how long (we need 90-days retention cap by default unless otherwise negotiated).
- SOC2: we accept time-limited portal access. Please send the DocuSign link for the portal NDA and a secure artifact upload link.

We can do Thu 10am PT. I'll invite an engineer and our procurement manager to the call; Raj will be on the line for the runbook discussion.

Thanks — Sarah
